checked.claim: Echoes (listen.echoes) is answered on the primary with no read of its one-action price, so a console write asks it free and as often as it likes; murder.park and murder.betrayal in an Eclipse are paid the same way, on the asker's browser.
checked.why: Read the whole road. The row's guards are knownSender, notSpectator, guardUndoIsTheGms and owns; none reads a payment. handleEchoes hands the actor alone to echoesFor, and echoesFor/echoesRefusal read the Eclipse, the clock's phase, the incident, the GMs' death record and the map - no action count, no ticket. The price is spent only in performEchoes on the asking browser before the ask. claimTicket exists for exactly a no-roll paid part (friskAsk, CLAIMED_ONLY) and Echoes is not among its kinds (no 'echoes' in roll-draw.mjs, sheet-audit.mjs, actions.mjs, bridge-guards.mjs). Not spending is no write, so the sheet audit sees nothing. The suite pins the reader's reading rather than the opposite: tier 2's E69-T6 judges a player's listen.echoes packet straight through G.judge with no payment made and expects a room. 30-security's E69 part sends Echoes only for another player's character. docs/dev/e69/STATUS.md 'What a console can still do' and the trust model's 'What stays open' do not name it. The park and betrayal runs (handleParkMurder, handleBetrayal) likewise read no payment; the reader rightly scopes those as one free action, not repeated information. Severity minor holds: it needs a console write, and each answer is one room, no name or count, but repeated asks walk the random ties and the answer is read on the GMs' knowledge (hidden tokens left out, a death the GMs keep left out).

checked.claim: The twelve E69/E74/E93 asks pass `local` without `onPrimary`, so on a second GM their GM halves (doors, watch, tail, eavesdrop, facility) run on that browser although each says it runs on the primary; the eavesdrop's microphone settle and the facility's once-a-time-of-day queue are then not the primary's.
checked.why: The structure stands from source: createWaiter.request runs `local` on any GM unless onPrimary (bridge-guards.mjs:1947), and the twelve asks pass local alone, while the passage, lair and Frisk rows pass onPrimary. It is stronger than the reader wrote in one place: gm-stores.mjs says the eavesdrop store is 'Written, read and dropped by the primary alone', and on a second GM startEavesdrop/endEavesdrop skip settleBlock and tellOwners (both isPrimaryGm-gated), and the hook that would settle the voices (voice.mjs scheduleTrialVoices on drpgEavesdropChanged) returns at once off the primary, is fired by Hooks.callAll on the writing browser only, and the store's setting gmEavesdrops has no onChange on the primary. serialWrite is a module-level Map per browser (utils.mjs:409-415), so the facility check is not ordered across GMs. But the failure scenario as written does not happen: a GM's voice tile draws no Stop listening (myEavesdrop reads `{}` for a GM, so paintStopListening draws nothing), and the GM's list Who you hear (paintEavesdroppers) has lines only, no button; no GM-side caller of requestEavesdropStop was found. What remains needs a non-primary GM to perform a student's Listen, door, watch, tail or room action from a sheet (action-doors.mjs, action-watch.mjs, action-tail.mjs, action-facilities.mjs, action-listen.mjs call the asks; whether a GM does so in practice was not established), and for the facility race two presses at once. requestFacilityUse's own comment says 'a GM runs it on their own client', so for that row the local road is written as intended. The reader marked it suspected; it stays a question, not a measured finding.
